pr.title: Introduce Arena::try_alloc_from_iter.
pr.description: `alloc_from_iter` already collects the iterator for reentrancy. So adding an early exit for a fallible iterator integrates naturally into the code. This avoids the other solution to allocate and dump the allocation.
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The supplied PR is a semantics-preserving optimization/refactor, not a source-grounded incorrect transformation. The old JumpThreading code uses `self.iter().map_while(|c| f(c) ... )` plus an `all_ok` flag: `map_while` stops at the first `None`, the already-mapped prefix is placed in the arena, and `all_ok.then_some(...)` discards it and returns `None`. The new code uses `try_alloc_from_iter(self.iter().map(|c| f(c).ok_or(())))`: `collect::<Result<SmallVec<[T;8]>, E>>` also stops at the first `Err`, performs no arena copy, and returns `None` via `.ok()?`. Both versions therefore call `f` on exactly the same prefix, return `None`/`Err` on exactly the first failing element, and return the same slice on all-success and empty inputs. The old version's temporary arena allocation of the successful prefix is unobservable in the returned value (only bump-allocation state/addresses differ, which is explicitly out of scope). The PR text's mention of "allocate and dump the allocation" is merely the slower but still correct alternative it avoids; the frozen analysis's "genuinely incorrect rewrite" (allocating directly without staging, or retaining partial results) is hypothetical and is not what this PR's diff does. Manufacturing such a rewrite would not be the historical transformation. Hence no source-grounded original/incorrect pair can be validated.

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically slower transformation was the "allocate and dump the allocation" approach: `arena.alloc_from_iter(self.iter().map_while(...))` followed by `all_ok.then_some(...)`, which performed the arena allocation even when the fallible mapping failed and then threw the result away. A genuinely incorrect rewrite of this optimization would allocate directly while iterating without first collecting into a `SmallVec`, or would fail to short-circuit at the first `Err`, breaking the documented reentrancy/panic-safety invariant or retaining partial results instead of returning the error.
analysis.inputDomain: Fallible iterators over `Result<T, E>` whose items are to be placed into a contiguous arena slice, including iterators that may be empty, may error after an arbitrary prefix, or may reentrantly reference the same arena; for JumpThreading specifically, condition sets where `f(c)` returns `None`/`Err` for one or more conditions.
analysis.originalLogic: `TypedArena::alloc_from_iter` intentionally collects the iterator into a `SmallVec<[_; 8]>` before writing into the arena because the arena is reentrant and for panic safety. `ConditionSet::filter_map` in jump_threading used that API with `iter().map_while(|c| ...)` plus an `all_ok` flag: it allocated the successfully mapped prefix into the arena even when a later condition failed, then discarded the whole slice via `all_ok.then_some(ConditionSet(set))`.
pitfalls: Do not allocate into the arena while still iterating, even if the fallible iterator is expected to succeed.
Do not continue iterating after the first `Err` and do not return a partially filled slice.
Do not assume the fallible path can reuse the non-fallible fast case, because the minimum iterator length is unknown when erroring.
Preserve the zero-sized-type assertion and the `set_len(0)` forgetting step after the copy.
preconditions: The arena is reentrant, so the iterator must be fully consumed into a staging `SmallVec` before the arena allocation/copy.
The fallible operation must propagate the first error and return no arena slice.
On success with an empty iterator, return an empty slice (`Ok(&mut [])`).
The non-fallible `alloc_from_iter` must remain equivalent by wrapping items in `Ok::<T, !>` and calling `into_ok()`.
analysis.summary: For fallible arena slice construction (and JumpThreading's condition-set mapping), collect the `Result` iterator into the staging `SmallVec` first so an early `Err` short-circuits before any arena write, then move the successful items into the arena. This preserves reentrancy and panic safety while avoiding the old allocate-then-discard behavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Add Rust unit tests for `try_alloc_from_iter`: an all-`Ok` iterator should produce the same slice contents as `alloc_from_iter`; an iterator that yields `Err` after a known prefix should return that `Err`, consume no further items (use a side-effect counter to confirm short-circuit), and leave no observable arena entries. Include an empty iterator case returning an empty slice, and a reentrancy case where the iterator itself allocates from the same arena. For JumpThreading, test `ConditionSet::filter_map` with a condition mapping that fails partway and assert the result is `None` rather than a set containing the successful prefix.
analysis.trigger: A pass wants to map an iterator into arena-allocated values but the mapping is fallible and must abort the whole allocation on the first failure; the existing `alloc_from_iter` cannot express early exit.
